$comment: The single corpus behind every subject-shape check. Loaded by pytest (BFF) and vitest (UI) so a regex that drifts in one language fails that language's tests. Standard: subject-naming.md. Decision: ADR-0023.
patternNote: Deliberately uses non-capturing groups only. Named groups are spelled (?P<n>...) in Python and (?<n>...) in JavaScript, so a pattern carrying them cannot be shared by both. Each caller adds its own named groups if it needs the parts; this string is the portable shape check.
claimedNote: `claimed` says whether the SERVER RULE judges this subject, which is not the same question as whether the pattern matches it. The registry holds artifacts governed by other standards, so the rule judges a subject only when its third segment is one of `types` — the evidence of claiming this grammar. claimed=false means the rule must stay silent (flagging it would make the compliance verdict lie about an artifact the rule has no authority over); claimed=true means it must fail. Every entry in `invalid` is rejected by `pattern` either way. The strict check across the whole repository, which knows the full out-of-scope allowlist, is a repo test instead.
